answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identities forge reputation only through costly, verifiable work: before trading, each identity must complete attested tasks that burn compute, and its standing grows only from completed jobs. Newcomers start in a low-trust oasis where transaction sizes are capped and histories are public; earning full access requires a juniper-slow record of attestations over weeks. A farmer spawning a thousand fake identities must pay the work cost and wait out the growth period for each one, so faking a crowd costs a thousand times more than joining honestly.
